title: The coax output style puts each command for the person to run in its own code block
body:
coax draws a copy button on every fenced code block, and nowhere else. `Rendered::copy_text` in `ui.rs` returns the block's text. The coax output style under coax-3d286f, in both `coax.md` and the `coax-next.md` draft, says to put commands in inline code and says nothing about commands meant for the person to run. Claude then puts such a command in inline code, which has no copy button. Or it puts several commands in one block with `#` comments above each, so a copy takes the comments along with the commands.

## Proposal

The style gets a section on commands for the person to run:

- Each command goes in its own fenced block, tagged `bash`.
- The block holds exactly what to paste. That means no `$` prompt, no `#` comment and no output.
- What the command does goes in the prose before the block.
- Output shown for comparison goes in a separate block tagged `text`.
- Inline code stays for naming a command in a sentence.

## Open

- Does a multi-line unit, such as a heredoc or a loop, count as one command and stay in one block? I lean yes, since splitting it would break the paste.
